inspection_summary: The complete source strengthens the Nyman-Beurling closure criterion from the full real dilation family to the natural-indexed family. It diagnoses the failure and unavoidable slowness of direct Möbius approximants, replaces them by an epsilon-weighted Dirichlet family, and uses a Fourier-Mellin representation to separate the Riemann-hypothesis-dependent finite-sum limit that establishes membership in the natural Beurling space from the unconditional epsilon-to-zero limit that reaches the characteristic function. All 377 lines were inspected. Exact symbolic claims are withheld where the normalized text visibly corrupts formula layout, especially the abstract's dilation formula, the displayed gamma quotient, and the stated domain of the transform space.

accepted_units.title: Replacing continuous dilation freedom by natural dilations
accepted_units.why_material: The source sharpens a Hilbert-space closure criterion equivalent to the Riemann hypothesis: membership of the interval characteristic function in the span generated by all admissible real dilations can be replaced by membership in the much thinner span generated by natural-indexed dilations. This is the paper's central semantic change, turning a continuous approximation family into a discrete one without weakening the criterion.
accepted_units.context_note: The span definitions, the original criterion, the strengthened theorem, and the explicit comparison of the two spaces are kept together. Page furniture at lines 51-59 does not contribute mathematics but lies inside the coherent source span.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The prose and displayed membership statements support the criterion, but the extracted argument of the fractional-part function at lines 34-37 is typographically damaged; verify the scan before reusing its exact notation.

accepted_units.title: Why direct natural Möbius approximants require regularization
accepted_units.why_material: The naive natural Möbius partial sums have useful pointwise and restricted L1 behavior yet diverge in the ambient Hilbert space. Proposed subsequences and logarithmic mollification do not remove a general lower bound showing that any bounded-scale Beurling approximation can approach the target only slowly. Together these facts motivate changing the summation mechanism rather than merely enlarging a cutoff.
accepted_units.context_note: The unit begins after the natural span has been defined and retains the naive sums, two attempted repairs, and the approximation-rate obstruction that motivates the next construction.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The semantic contrast is explicit in prose. The displayed coefficients and lower bound are legible at the relation level, but formula typography should be checked against the scan before exact quantitative transcription.

accepted_units.title: An epsilon-weighted Möbius family as a reciprocal-zeta correction
accepted_units.why_material: Introducing a complex exponent weights the entire natural dilation range in a single family. For fixed spatial input the family is described as meromorphic and as a finite correction of the reciprocal zeta function, which makes analytic information available to the approximation problem. The proof plan is explicitly split: under the Riemann hypothesis establish that each small positive-parameter limit remains in the natural span, then unconditionally let the parameter tend to zero in the Hilbert norm.
accepted_units.context_note: This span contains the construction, its analytic interpretation, and both announced limiting obligations; retaining them together prevents the later conditional and unconditional steps from being conflated.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The finite-correction identity at lines 108-111 has damaged bracket and fraction layout. The surrounding prose supports the correction mechanism and two-stage plan, but the exact identity requires scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Zero-free half-planes control truncated reciprocal-zeta sums
accepted_units.why_material: The quoted Balazard-Saias estimate converts nonvanishing of zeta in a half-plane into uniform control of truncated Möbius Dirichlet sums relative to the reciprocal zeta function in an interior strip. This is the bridge later used to dominate the transformed finite natural approximants under the Riemann hypothesis.
accepted_units.context_note: The introductory attribution and full lemma statement are included because they specify both the hypothesis and the strip in which the approximation is available.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The estimate is formula-dependent and its exponents and parameter names are crowded by extraction. Its directional role is secure from the prose, but exact bounds require comparison with the scan.

accepted_units.title: A functional-equation bound independent of the Riemann hypothesis
accepted_units.why_material: A second lemma bounds a zeta quotient along vertical lines uniformly over a small parameter range and explicitly does not assume the Riemann or Lindelöf hypotheses. Its proof route passes through the zeta functional equation and gamma asymptotics, furnishing the unconditional domination needed for the outer parameter limit.
accepted_units.context_note: The independence claim, bound, proof mechanism, and stated source of the asymptotics are retained as one unit.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The displayed gamma quotient at lines 155-157 is visibly corrupt and cannot support exact symbolic reconstruction. Only the prose-grounded functional-equation-to-gamma-asymptotics mechanism and the separately displayed zeta-ratio bound are accepted; scan verification is required for the intermediate identity.

accepted_units.title: Weighted natural sums produce two nested pointwise limits
accepted_units.why_material: The proof defines finite natural Beurling sums with an epsilon weight. Passing the cutoff to infinity uses the reciprocal-zeta term plus a finite correction to identify a pointwise limit, and then passing epsilon to zero uses the fundamental Möbius cancellation property to identify the target as the negative characteristic function. This exposes the two limits whose norm convergence must be proved separately.
accepted_units.context_note: The unit includes the construction, both pointwise identifications, and the explicit statement that Hilbert-norm convergence remains the unresolved task.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The argument depends on displayed finite sums, floor-like brackets, and reciprocal-zeta factors whose layout has extraction artifacts. The order and identities of the two limits are supported by prose; exact formula transcription needs the scan.

accepted_units.title: Fourier-Mellin isometry turns closure into transform-space domination
accepted_units.why_material: The proof changes representation from the original Hilbert space to an isometric Fourier-Mellin transform space. A Mellin identity for the basic Beurling function factors the transform of a weighted finite approximant into a zeta factor and a truncated Möbius Dirichlet sum, so Littlewood's theorem identifies the transformed pointwise limit. This is the structural move that makes analytic estimates usable as norm-convergence evidence.
accepted_units.context_note: The target transform space, isometry, root Mellin identity, transformed finite sum, and pointwise transform limit are kept together despite intervening page furniture.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Line 201 gives the transform-space interval as '(∞, ∞)', which is extraction-defective, and several exponents in lines 219-233 are crowded. The prose securely states invertible isometry and factorization roles, but the exact domain and formulas must be scan-checked.

accepted_units.title: Riemann-hypothesis domination yields natural-space membership
accepted_units.why_material: With the zero-free parameter specialized to the critical boundary, the proof combines the truncated reciprocal-zeta estimate, the Lindelöf consequence of the Riemann hypothesis, and the unconditional quotient bound to produce an integrable transform-space majorant. Dominated convergence then gives norm convergence of weighted finite natural sums; separate control on the regions below and above one removes the auxiliary spatial weight, placing the limiting function in the closed natural Beurling space.
accepted_units.context_note: The entire conditional chain is retained from estimate selection through transform-space convergence, removal of the multiplier, and the membership conclusion.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The logical chain is stated in prose, but exact decay powers, quotient layout, and the bound at lines 268-271 are formula-sensitive and should be verified from the scan before quantitative reuse.

accepted_units.title: The unconditional outer limit closes the strengthened criterion
accepted_units.why_material: After the Riemann hypothesis has supplied natural-space membership for each small positive parameter, the identified transform limit and the hypothesis-free quotient bound give Hilbert convergence as the parameter tends to zero. The previously established pointwise identification fixes the norm limit as the negative characteristic function, and closure then supplies the theorem's nontrivial implication.
accepted_units.context_note: The overlap with the preceding unit is intentional: line 279 marks the transition from membership of each regularized limit to the separate outer-limit argument. The conclusion is kept with the unconditional mechanism.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The transform quotient at lines 282-284 has compact, noisy typography. The unconditional status and convergence conclusion are explicit in prose, while exact transform notation requires scan verification.

accepted_units.title: A convergence criterion and a proposed Lp extension
accepted_units.why_material: The author records that the proof also gives a route to the original Nyman-Beurling criterion without the cited Hardy-space machinery and states an exact corollary: the Riemann hypothesis is equivalent to Hilbert-norm convergence of the regularized finite sums for every sufficiently small positive parameter. An analogous Lp zero-free-half-plane criterion is explicitly presented as something to extend the proof to, not as an established theorem.
accepted_units.context_note: The proved consequence and proposed generalization are colocated so their different evidential status can be preserved.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: This unit is supported mainly by prose and the corollary statement; the source provides no proof of the proposed Lp extension.

accepted_units.title: Summability, subsequence criteria, and a possible rate-sensitive refinement
accepted_units.why_material: The construction is interpreted as a summability method applied to the old natural approximation. Convergence along special cutoff and regularization-parameter subsequences is said to remain necessary and sufficient, motivating comparison with other summability procedures. The unused cutoff dependence in the technical estimate is then suggested as potentially connected to the known slowness of approximation.
accepted_units.context_note: This final mathematical comment links the paper's mechanism back to the earlier failure mode and identifies a source-specific direction for refinement.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The connection between cutoff dependence and slow approximation is explicitly tentative ('would seem'), so it is retained as a proposed relation rather than a proved claim.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Regularization as a bridge from discrete closure to reciprocal-zeta control
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The source answers failure of direct natural Möbius partial sums by introducing an analytic weight whose Fourier-Mellin image exposes a reciprocal-zeta Dirichlet approximation; zero-free-region control can then be converted into closure of the natural dilation span.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: This is a source-internal proof mechanism, not evidence that every summability scheme or every discrete approximation admits the same analytic bridge; exact displayed formulas require scan verification.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: A two-limit architecture with different logical dependencies
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The cutoff limit and the regularization-parameter limit perform distinct jobs: the Riemann hypothesis is used to place each regularized limit in the natural space, while the subsequent convergence of those limits to the target is obtained without that hypothesis once the transform bound and pointwise identity are available.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The synthesis records the proof's direction under the Riemann hypothesis; the reverse implication still relies on the already stated Nyman-Beurling criterion and containment of the natural span in the full span.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Convergence criteria inherit the summability method
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Because the analytic weighting turns the old natural approximation into a convergent family precisely under the criterion, convergence of the regularized finite sums becomes an equivalent formulation and motivates subsequence and alternative-summability variants.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The source states the small-parameter convergence corollary and the special-subsequence equivalence, but only proposes broader summability study and an Lp extension.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Approximation slowness may be encoded in unused cutoff dependence
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The early lower bound establishes slow approximation, while the final comment points to the cutoff-dependent error in the zero-free-region estimate as a possible place where that slowness is analytically reflected.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The source labels this connection as suggestive and does not derive a quantitative rate relation.
